analysis: The code snippet reads lines from an InputStream, and for each non-empty line, it calls readMultiplePolygons(current, mapping). According to the provided exception information, readMultiplePolygons may throw java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException due to malformed input (from charAt and substring). It may also throw other runtime exceptions from the add method (UnsupportedOperationException, IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException). The current code only catches IOException and performs System.exit(0) on IOException. No runtime exceptions are caught. The runtime exceptions, especially IndexOutOfBoundsException, are foreseeable and should be handled to avoid program crash. The best optimization is to catch IndexOutOfBoundsException within the loop structure, so that a malformed line can be skipped and processing can continue. Adding a single try-catch structure inside the while loop around the readMultiplePolygons call achieves this.
